fields.Page Content:
Drill: 1vs1 After Pass

Setup

  • 2 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2.
  2. Player 2 passes back into the run of Player 1.
  3. Right after the pass, Player 2 takes defensive position.
  4. Player 1 attacks the goal in a 1vs1 situation.

Player Roles

  • Player 1: attack with speed after receiving the return pass.
  • Player 2: must react quickly and defend directly after the pass.

Coaching Points

  • Attack with speed and control.
  • Defending player must close space fast.
  • Focus on 1vs1 duels: attacker creativity vs. defender positioning.

Variations

  • Start drill from both sides.
  • Limit attacker to max. 5 seconds or staying on it’s horizontal half of the field
  • Defender has to reach a certain point to simulate more offensive defending
fields.Name: 1 vs 1 from Middleline

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1 in the corner

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2 (on the side).
  2. Player 2 passes down to Player 3 (low corner).
  3. Player 3 passes into the middle, where Player 1 has moved after the first pass.
  4. Player 1 gives the ball back to Player 3.
  5. Player 3 now has 3 choices:
    • Option 1: Shoot directly.
    • Option 2: Pass to the long post, where Player 2 is moving.
    • Option 3: Pass up to the high slot.

Player Roles

  • Player 2 always goes to the net for rebound.
  • Player 1 must move into the high slot after the first pass.
  • Player 3 is the decision maker: shoot or pass.

Coaching Points

  • Passquality is key
  • Timing is important: players must move right after their pass.
  • Rebounds: Player 2 must be ready.
  • Encourage quick and direct passes

Variations

  • Mirror the drill after several executions or minutes
  • Play only one-touch passes for speed.
fields.Name: Quick Passes with Shot from Slot

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2.
  2. Player 2 passes back to Player 1 → and then becomes the defender.
  3. Player 1 attacks in a 1vs1 situation.
  4. After the 1vs1 is finished, Player 3 joins as a second attacker with the ball.
  5. Now Player 1 + Player 3 play a 2vs1 against Player 2.
  6. The 2vs1 should be played fast — max. 2 passes before the shot.

Player Roles

  • Player 1: attacker in both situations. First solo in 1vs1, then combine with Player 3.
  • Player 2: defender, must switch quickly from pass into defense.
  • Player 3: new attacker, starts with dribbling into the 2vs1.

Coaching Points

  • 1v1: Player 1 should attack with speed and try to create space for a shot.
  • Defender: must react fast after passing, close the gap early to find positioning.
  • 2vs1: play quick, simple — one or two passes, then finish.
  • Attackers should keep good spacing (not too close together).

Variations

  • Limit attackers to only one pass or a shot in 2vs1.
  • Defender can start with a small delay for more pressure on attackers.
fields.Name: 1vs1 into 2vs1

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1 in the corner

Sequence

  1. Player 1 dribbles a few meters with the ball.
  2. Player 1 passes to Player 2 (middle).
  3. Player 2 passes back to Player 1, who has moved to a new position.
  4. Player 1 passes across to Player 3 on the weak side.
  5. Player 3 takes a direct shot.
  6. Player 2 goes for the rebound.

Player Roles

  • Player 1 must move directly after the first pass.
  • Player 2 gives the ball back quickly and then crashes the net.
  • Player 3 should be ready for a one-touch shot.

Coaching Points

  • Focus on direct passes and shots.
  • Move immediately after passing.
  • Rebounds: Player 2 must be ready.
  • Encourage quick execution (1–2 touches).

Variations

  • Mirror the drill after several executions or minutes
  • Require all passes and shots to be one-touch.
fields.Name: Move after Pass from Corner

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1

Sequence

  1. Player 1 dribbles 2–3 meters.
  2. Player 1 passes while moving to Player 2.
  3. Player 2 dribbles behind the goal and passes out to Player 3.
  4. Player 3 comes in full movement and shoots.

Player Roles

  • Player 1: quick pass and then move forward for possible rebound.
  • Player 2: keep speed behind the net, pass at the right moment.
  • Player 3: time the run well, shoot directly in movement.

Coaching Points

  • Focus on timing: Player 3 should arrive in full speed for the shot.
  • Encourage different shot types (sweeper, slapshot).
  • Passes must be direct and easy to control.
  • Good movement after each pass.

Variations

  • Add Player 1 and/or Player 2 as rebounders in front of the goal.
  • Mirror the drill after several executions or minutes
  • Make Player 2 a defender and Player 1 the attacker for a additional 1vs1 in front of the goal
fields.Name: Distance Shot from Movement

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 2 field players (Red 1 and Red 2) + 1 chasing player (Blue 1) + goalie
  • Cones placed at the middle to guide movement
  • Balls start with Red 2 at center

Sequence

  1. Red 1 starts near the goal and moves forward.
  2. Blue 1 follows Red 1 to chase.
  3. Red 1 makes two scans to see where Blue 2 is.
  4. Blue 2 passes to Red 1 between the cones.
  5. Red 1 controls the ball directly and dribbles around the cone.
  6. Blue 2 runs around the other cone and then backchecks to defend.
  7. Drill finishes with a 1v0 situation for Red 1 and Blue 1.

Roatation

Red 1 → Blue 1 Red 2 → Red 1 Blue 1 → Red 2

Player Roles

  • Red 1: must scan before receiving, quick control, attack fast.
  • Blue 1: follows and adds backcheck pressure.
  • Red 2: quality pass with right timing.
  • Goalie: positioning give the attacker a bad angle, go out in the right moments

Coaching Points

  • Red 1 must scan twice before the pass.
  • First touch is important: take it forward into open space.
  • Attack with speed before the backchecker catches up.
  • Blue 2 must sprint hard to apply real pressure.

Variations

-
fields.Name: Scan and Breakaway with Backcheck

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • min 6 players & 1–2 goalies
  • Every shift starts with a 3 vs 3

Sequence

  1. The game is played as normal 3 vs 3 on one, two, or more goals. Both teams can score on all goals
  2. As soon as a player scores, that player must leave the field immediately.
  3. The scoring team continues playing with one player less.

Player Roles

  • Players: focus on decision making and scanning for the next best action and free teammates.
  • Goalie: control rebounds and protect the goal area.

Rotation

  • Play for 30 seconds, then the next 3 players from each team enter the field directly.
  • The game ends if a team has no players left on the field during one shift.
  • This means the team scored at least 3 goals in that shift (very unlikely, but possible).

Coaching Points

  • Decision making: find free scoring chances quickly.
  • Focus on physical duels rather than stick duels.

Variations

  • Place goals on both ends of the field to widen the space
  • Move the goals very close together to create one large scoring area.
  • Add more than two goals

  • Every shift starts with a 3 vs 3
  • min 6 players + 1–2 goalies
fields.Name: Championship Ball (Score & Leave)

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Goalie starts with the ball (throw into corner)
  • 4 players active (2 red, 2 black)
  • 2 more players waiting (Player 3 red & black)
  • Play in one half of the filed

Sequence

  1. Goalie throws the ball into one corner.
  2. Player 2 (red) and Player 1 (black) have a 1vs1 in the corner
  3. As soon as the ball leaves the corner or one player wins control → the drill continues as a 2vs2 with both pairs (Red 1 + Red 2 vs. Black 1 + Black 2).
  4. In the 2 vs 2 they are allowed to pass to the joker of their color to make it a 3 vs 2 advantage
  5. 3 vs 2 situation should be played quick with a shot on the goal to

Player Roles

  • Corner players (Red 2 & Black 1): must win the corner 1 vs 1.
  • Support players (Red 1 & Black 2): must be ready to join as soon as ball comes out.
  • Extra players (Red 3 & Black 3): come as Jokers in the game. They should lead to quick chance

Coaching Points

  • Intensity in the corner is key.
  • Quick decisions after winning the ball (pass, dribble,).
  • Support players must move into good positions, not stand still.
  • Communication between teammates to handle transition from 1vs1 → 2vs2 → 3vs2.

Variations

  • Allow goalie to throw into both corners to change start point.
  • Add time limit: must shoot within 10 seconds.
  • Play to goals or set a point system (winning the corner duel = 1 point, scoring = 2 points).
fields.Name: 1 vs 1, 2vs2, 3 vs 2

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players
  • 2 cones placed in a line about 5–6 meters apart
  • No Goalies

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2, who receives the ball while moving.
  2. Player 2 makes a 180 degree sweep pass around the cone to the other side to Player 3.
  3. After the pass, Player 2 runs to the diagnollay mirrored same position as before, receives the ball and continuous the infinite cycle of passing.

Coaching Points

  • Keep movement smooth, close to the cone, with high speed and pass timing
  • Use this drill as a warmup before shot practice with sweeper shots
  • Run for about 1 minute per round, then switch the player in the middle.
    • We recommend 2 rounds per player with 1 min as the second round usually has higher quality

Variations

  • Players should keep eye contact and avoid looking down at the ball.
fields.Name: Pass like Gabriel Kohonen

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1 (corner position)

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2 and immediately runs toward Player 3.
  2. Player 2 makes a direct pass to Player 3.
  3. Player 3 plays a short one-two pass (give and go) with the moving Player 1.
  4. After the one-two, Player 3 has three options:
    1. Option 1: Shoot on goal. Player 2 goes for the rebound.
    2. Option 2: Pass into the high slot to Player 1. Player 1 shoots and Player 2 goes for the rebound.
    3. Option 3: Cross pass to Player 2 for a direct shot.

Rotation

  • After each round:
    • Player 1 moves to Player 3’s position.
    • Player 2 moves to Player 1’s position.
    • Player 3 moves to Player 2’s position.

Goalies

  • Read Player 3 and try to predict the next action based on body, blade, … .

Coaching Points

  • Focus on timing of passes and player movement.
  • Quick and clean passes.
  • Players and goalies should take the blade side and field position into account when making decisions.
  • Force the goalie to actively anticipate the player’s decision.

Variations

  • After the one-two, Player 1 becomes a defender against Player 2 and Player 3 (2vs1 situation).
  • Run the drill from both sides.
fields.Name: Options in the Slot

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 4 players + goalie
  • Balls start with Player 1 in the corner

Sequence

  1. Player 1 and Player 2 play a double pass.
  2. Player 2 passes cross to Player 3.
  3. Player 3 passes directly down to Player 4.
  4. Player 1 moves into the slot to get into a shooting position.
  5. Player 4 passes to Player 1, who finishes with a direct shot from the slot.

Player Roles

  • Player 1 moves into a good scoring position.
  • Goalie read the ball and player movement early and adjust position proactively to focus on correct angle on the final pass.

Rotation

Player 1 → Player 4

Player 4 → Player 3

Player 3 → Player 2

Player 2 → Player 1

Coaching Points

  • Focus on timing of passes and player movement
  • Pass quality is key.

Variations

  • Mirror the drill after several rounds and start from the opposite corner.
  • Remove the double pass for a version with more ball speed
  • Add rules (e.g., direct passes, mandatory direct shot).
  • Add running game e.g. for Player 1 and Player 4.
  • Make it a 2 vs 0 with Player 1 and Player 4.
  • Use Player 2 as a defender to pressure Player 1 from behind.
  • Use Player 2 as a second scoring option on the second post.
fields.Name: Move the Ball into Scoring Position

fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players with 2 balls
  • 1 goalie

Sequence

  1. Player 1 plays a cross pass to Player 2.
  2. Player 2 holds the ball while Player 1 starts moving.
  3. After 3–5 meters, Player 1 turns and plays a double pass with Player 3.
  4. Player 1 turns again, receives a pass from Player 2, and takes the first shot.
  5. Player 1 continues the movement and receives a pass from Player 3 in the slot for a second shot.

Player Roles

  • Focus on technique and skill, especially good pass quality.
  • Player 3 must always be ready to pass and react.

Rotation

  • Change the side after the shots.
  • The drill always starts from the opposite side.

Coaching Points

  • Continuous movement after each shot by Player 1.
  • All players must stay ready, especially Player 3.
  • To make it harder increase passing speed

Variations

  • Only a direct shots allowed
  • 2nd pass with speed to the slot so that Player 1 only has to tip it
fields.Name: Double Shot
Build up behind the goal with shot

fields.Page Content:
You can play this drill in many different variations and also with more players, for example 5vs2 or 6vs2.

A good rule of thumb: in a 4vs1 situation, players should use one touch, and in a 4vs2 situation, players are allowed two touches to receive and play the ball.

As soon as a defender wins the ball, the positions change.

With two defenders, you can also rotate so that the player who has been in the middle the longest goes out.
fields.Name: Rondo
Diagonal one-two with finish in slot

fields.Page Content: Drill for multiple shots in one round. Mirror the drill after a time so that you develop lefties and righties the same and they stay happy
fields.Name: Shooting Positions

fields.Page Content:
Move the goals to a distance of around 20 meters.

This is a passing and shooting drill with a high cadence, ideal for the last training before a game to keep intensity and scoring confidence high.

Easy to introduce competitive challenges between both groups.
fields.Name: Crosspass

fields.Page Content: Drill to practice the opening via a middle player can be used to practice timing on the different movements of the players
fields.Name: Opening over the Middle

fields.Page Content:
One player stands in the middle of a square marked with different colored or numbered cones (distance 3–4 meters).

The coach or another player calls out a color or number.

The player in the middle moves toward the called cone without losing eye contact, receives the pass, and plays it directly back with one touch.

Run the drill for 45 seconds per round.

We recommend using flat cones to make passing easier.
fields.Name: Color Passing

fields.Page Content: Move the goals to a distance of around 20 meters and run the drill with high intensity in backcheck
fields.Name: Transition with Backcheck
